title_en: Xing Furong v. Beijing Dingdian Taifu Investment Management Co., Ltd., Ding Shiguo, et al. — dispute over transfer of partnership property shares
ruling_gist_en: The special agreement in the partnership agreement regarding the transfer of partnership property shares does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, nor does it contravene public order and good customs. It should be recognized as lawful and valid, and the partners shall strictly comply with such agreement. Where the partnership agreement has expressly stipulated that the transfer of partnership property shares between partners requires the unanimous consent of all partners, before other partners have consented to the transfer of partnership property shares, the transfer agreement concluded between the parties for the transfer of partnership property shares is formed but not yet effective. If other partners explicitly do not consent to the transfer of such partnership property shares, then the transfer agreement is definitively ineffective and cannot create enforceability between the parties. If a party requests the performance of the transfer agreement, the people's court shall not support such request.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over transfer of partnership property shares; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; Jilin Province; Natural person; Legal person; Partnership Enterprise Law; Validity of special agreements in partnership agreements; Formation and effectiveness of property share transfer agreements; Enforceability of contract; Reversal of judgment; Transfer of partnership property shares; Partnership agreement stipulating unanimous consent of all partners; Transfer agreement not yet effective; Public order and good customs
full_text_en:
Xing Furong v. Beijing Dingdian Taifu Investment Management Co., Ltd., Ding Shiguo, et al.

— Dispute over transfer of partnership property shares

【Ruling Summary】

Special provisions in a partnership agreement regarding the transfer of partnership property shares, which do not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, nor contravene public order and good customs, shall be deemed lawful and valid, and partners must strictly comply with such provisions. Where a partnership agreement expressly stipulates that the transfer of partnership property shares between partners requires the unanimous consent of all partners, a transfer agreement signed by the parties for the transfer of partnership property shares is established but not yet effective before the other partners have consented to the transfer. If the other partners explicitly disagree with the transfer of the partnership property shares, the transfer agreement is definitively ineffective and cannot create a binding obligation between the parties. Where a party requests performance of the transfer agreement, the People's Court shall not support such request.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2020) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Judgment No. 904

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing Dingdian Taifu Investment Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 402, 4th Floor, Building 49, No. 10 Langjiayuan, Jianguomenwai, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Ding Shiguo, Executive Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Xue, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Jian, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Xing Furong, female, born July 15, 1968, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Agent ad litem: Li Qingming, Attorney at Law, Beijing Dacheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Linsen, Attorney at Law, Beijing Dacheng Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Ding Shiguo, male, born October 12, 1979, Han ethnicity, domiciled in Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Agent ad litem: Li Xue, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Jian, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Dingdian Investment Management (Beijing) Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 403, 4th Floor, Building 49, No. 10 Langjiayuan, Jianguomenwai, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Ding Shiguo, Executive Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Xue, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Jian, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Jilin Province Investment Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 1166 Renmin Street, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Jingyou, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Shubo, Attorney at Law, Jilin Changchun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yan, Attorney at Law, Jilin Changchun Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Jiaxing Zeyuan Equity Investment Partnership (Limited Partnership). Business Premises: Room 5533, 5th Floor, Building 10, Chuangye South Road, Nanhu District, Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province.

Managing Partner: Dingdian Investment Management (Beijing) Co., Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Li Xue, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Jian, Attorney at Law, Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

The appellant, Beijing Dingdian Taifu Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dingdian Taifu Company), appealed against the civil judgment (2019) Jimin Chu No. 5 rendered by the Jilin High People's Court in the case of dispute over transfer of partnership property shares with the appellee Xing Furong and the defendants at first instance Ding Shiguo, Dingdian Investment Management (Beijing) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dingdian Investment Company), Jilin Province Investment Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jilin Investment Company), and Jiaxing Zeyuan Equity Investment Partnership (hereinafter referred to as Jiaxing Zeyuan), and filed an appeal with this Court. After accepting the case, this Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on September 9, 2020. The joint agents ad litem of Dingdian Taifu Company, Ding Shiguo, Dingdian Investment Company, and Jiaxing Zeyuan — Li Xue and Zhao Jian; the agent ad litem of Xing Furong — Liu Linsen; and the agents ad litem of Jilin Investment Company — Zhang Shubo and Liu Yan — appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

Dingdian Taifu Company appealed with the following requests: to set aside the judgment of first instance, to dismiss all of Xing Furong's claims, and to order Xing Furong to bear the litigation costs. Facts and grounds: (1) According to Article 22 of the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Partnership Enterprise Law) and the provisions of the Partnership Agreement of Jilin Province National New Energy Venture Capital Fund Partnership (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as the Partnership Agreement), the transfer of Xing Furong's partnership shares required the unanimous consent of all partners. The Agreement on Transfer of Partnership Property Shares (hereinafter referred to as the Transfer Agreement) signed between Xing Furong and Dingdian Taifu Company on January 5, 2018, was not unanimously consented to by all partners, violating the mandatory provisions of the said law, and should be void. The court of first instance erred in law by holding the Transfer Agreement lawful and valid. (2) The Transfer Agreement violated Article 15 of Chapter 4 of the Interim Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Privately Offered Investment Funds, which provides that "private fund managers and private fund sales institutions shall not promise investors that their investment principal will not suffer losses or promise a minimum return," thereby harming the healthy development of the private investment fund industry and contravening public order and good customs, and therefore should be void. (3) According to Article 4 of the Transfer Agreement, Dingdian Taifu Company was entitled to terminate the Transfer Agreement. The operating term of Jilin Province National New Energy Venture Capital Fund Partnership (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as the New Energy Fund) expired on November 26, 2019, and it has been dissolved and is in liquidation. The purpose of the Transfer Agreement cannot be achieved, and Dingdian Taifu Company is no longer able to acquire Xing Furong's partnership property shares, thus the basis for Dingdian Taifu Company to pay the transfer price no longer exists. (4) Xing Furong added a claim for liquidated damages after the conclusion of the first-instance trial, which should not have been supported. The court of first instance erred in law by finding that Xing Furong did not constitute an addition of a claim.

Xing Furong argued in response: (1) The Transfer Agreement is lawful and valid. (a) The Transfer Agreement does not constitute a guarantee of minimum return. The New Energy Fund was established on November 27, 2012, the Partnership Agreement was signed and the fund was registered with the Asset Management Association of China in April 2014, and the Transfer Agreement between Xing Furong and Dingdian Taifu Company was signed on January 5, 2018, nearly four years after the signing of the Partnership Agreement and fund registration. From these facts, it is evident that the Transfer Agreement was a mutual agreement reached between Xing Furong and Dingdian Taifu Company gradually after the establishment of the New Energy Fund regarding the transfer of partnership property shares, and not a guarantee of minimum return made by Dingdian Taifu Company to Xing Furong at the time of her investment in the New Energy Fund. Moreover, the Interim Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Privately Offered Investment Funds is a departmental regulation, constituting a regulatory mandatory provision rather than a validity mandatory provision. Therefore, the Transfer Agreement does not constitute a guarantee of minimum return and does not contravene public order and good customs. (b) Although Dingdian Taifu Company claims that it is an industry practice that a general partner cannot hold more than 2% of partnership shares, it has not provided evidence to prove this, and in fact, there is no such industry practice. Furthermore, industry practices are informal sources of law and are supplements to statutory law. They can only serve as the basis for adjudication where legislation recognizes them or where there is a legal gap. Therefore, Dingdian Taifu Company's claim that the Transfer Agreement violates industry practices and should be void is unfounded in fact. (c) The Transfer Agreement reflects the true intent of both parties and does not involve duress or other voidable grounds. Moreover, Dingdian Taifu Company has repeatedly confirmed in writing its willingness to perform its contractual obligations. (2) The Transfer Agreement can still be performed. (a) The restrictions on the transfer of partnership shares in the Partnership Agreement do not affect the performance of the Transfer Agreement. Article 22(2) of the Partnership Enterprise Law provides: "When a partner transfers all or part of its property shares in the partnership to another partner, it shall notify the other partners." This provision does not stipulate that the partnership agreement may impose additional restrictions on the transfer of property shares between partners. Therefore, the provision in the Partnership Agreement requiring "unanimous consent of all partners" for the transfer of property shares between partners is inconsistent with the Partnership Enterprise Law. This provision objectively restricts the statutory right of partners to transfer property shares as conferred by the Partnership Enterprise Law, is completely unreasonable, and does not fall within the scope of matters that parties may freely agree upon. Thus, it is not binding on the parties, and the Transfer Agreement can still be performed. (b) The expiration of the New Energy Fund's operating term does not constitute a valid defense. Xing Furong filed the first-instance lawsuit on February 11, 2019. The expiration date of the New Energy Fund's term was November 26, 2019. Therefore, when Xing Furong filed this lawsuit, there was no obstacle to the realization of her rights and obligations. (c) Even if it is found that the transfer of partnership shares is subject to performance obstacles due to the lack of unanimous consent from all partners, Dingdian Taifu Company, as the general partner of the New Energy Fund, knew at the time of signing the above restriction on the transfer of partnership shares and should bear the risks itself. (3) The court of first instance did not adjudicate beyond the claims. After the first-instance trial, Xing Furong clarified that the amount due from July 1, 2018, to the date of actual payment constituted losses from delayed payment, calculated based on 50 million yuan as the principal at a rate of 50% above the benchmark loan interest rate for the same period. This change is a clarification of the facts and grounds of the claim and a specification of the method for calculating civil liability, and does not constitute a change in the claim itself. In conclusion, the appeal should be dismissed and the judgment of first instance affirmed.

Ding Shiguo, Dingdian Investment Company, and Jiaxing Zeyuan argued in defense that they agreed with the appeal requests, facts, and grounds of Dingdian Taifu Company.

Jilin Investment Company argued in defense that the court of first instance correctly found that Jilin Investment Company should not bear liability for compensation, and the findings of fact and application of law were correct.

Xing Furong filed the following claims with the court of first instance: (1) Dingdian Taifu Company should pay Xing Furong the transfer price of RMB 74,679,452 [calculated as: 50 million yuan x (1 + 8% x 2,252 days / 365 days), calculated provisionally from November 28, 2012, to January 28, 2019], and pay interest at the agreed annual rate of 8% until the full transfer price is paid; (2) Ding Shiguo, Dingdian Investment Company, Jilin Investment Company, and Jiaxing Zeyuan should each bear supplementary liability for the amount that Dingdian Taifu Company cannot pay, within the scope of their unpaid capital contributions and the interest thereon. The defendants should bear the litigation costs. After the first-instance trial, Xing Furong submitted a supplemental explanation regarding the first claim, clarifying that the amount claimed was the transfer price payable by Dingdian Taifu Company of RMB 72,356,164.38 (calculated as: 50 million yuan x 108% x 2,040 days / 365 days, calculated from November 28, 2012, to June 30, 2018), and losses for delayed payment (calculated at 50 million yuan as the principal, based on a rate of 50% above the benchmark loan interest rate for the same period, i.e., 7%, calculated from July 1, 2018, until the full payment is made).

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial: On November 27, 2012, the New Energy Fund was registered and established. In 2014, the partners Yingfuke Venture Capital Co., Ltd., Jilin Province Urban Construction Industrial Co., Ltd., Xing Furong, Jilin Province Venture Capital Guidance Fund Co., Ltd., Yingkou Hongjia Investment Co., Ltd., and Dingdian Taifu Company signed the Partnership Agreement. The main contents were: the enterprise was a limited partnership; Dingdian Taifu Company was the general partner, managing partner, and fund manager of the New Energy Partnership; the other parties were limited partners. The total capital contribution of the fund was RMB 262.63 million, all in cash. Except for Yingfuke Venture Capital Co., Ltd., the other partners were required to make a one-time payment of 100% of their subscribed capital contributions within 30 days after the Partnership Agreement took effect. Xing Furong subscribed a capital contribution of RMB 50 million, representing a subscription ratio of 19.04%. The operating term of the New Energy Partnership was the fund's duration, which was 7 years, calculated from the date of establishment, i.e., the date the business license was issued. The general partner (fund manager) had the right to convene, preside over, and attend the general meeting of partners and other partner meetings in accordance with the law, and exercise corresponding voting rights; if the managing partner failed to perform its duties, limited partners representing one-third or more of the total capital contribution had the right to convene and preside over meetings on their own and exercise corresponding voting rights. Article 27.6 of the Agreement stipulated: "Unless otherwise agreed, the following matters shall require the unanimous consent of all partners: ... (4) Transfer or pledge of property shares by limited partners ..." Article 33 stipulated: "Unless otherwise provided by law or a written decision unanimously agreed upon by all partners, a limited partner shall not be converted into a general partner, nor shall a general partner be converted into a limited partner."

On November 28, 2012, Xing Furong transferred RMB 50 million in capital contribution to the China Minsheng Bank account of the New Energy Fund.

In January 2018, Xing Furong (Party A) and Dingdian Taifu Company (Party B) signed the Transfer Agreement. Article 1 stipulated: "1. The subject matter of this Agreement refers to: Party A's 19.04% property shares in the New Energy Fund (totaling RMB 50 million). 2. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Party B agrees to assist Party A in seeking a third party to acquire Party A's 19.04% property shares in the New Energy Fund; the specific transfer price may be negotiated between Party A and the third party. 3. Party A warrants that its 19.04% property shares in the New Energy Fund can be legally transferred." Article 2 stipulated: "1. Both parties agree that, after this Agreement takes effect, until June 30, 2018, Party B may at any time contact a third party to negotiate with Party A regarding the specific terms of transfer until a transaction is reached; Party B may assist Party A in screening the transferee to ensure an annualized rate of return of not less than 6% and strive for an annualized rate of return of 8%; i.e., the transfer price shall be calculated as: 50 million yuan x 106% x actual number of days of fund use / 365 days (50 million yuan x 106% x actual number of days of fund use / 365 days); if no suitable third party acquires the property shares by December 31, 2018, after this Agreement takes effect, Party B undertakes to acquire the shares itself or designate a third party to acquire them directly; the transfer price between the parties shall be calculated to ensure an annualized rate of return of not less than 6% and strive for 8% as of June 30, 2018, i.e., the transfer price shall be calculated as: 50 million yuan x 106% x actual number of days of fund use / 365 days (or 50 million yuan x 108% x actual number of days of fund use / 365 days) ... 4. During this period, Party B may, based on the investment situation and overall conditions of the New Energy Fund, decide to terminate this Agreement at any time; if Party B decides to enjoy the exit proceeds from the New Energy Fund's projects, this Agreement shall terminate; if Party B continues to perform this Agreement, it shall not be entitled to enjoy the exit proceeds from the New Energy Fund's projects ..." Article 3 stipulated: "1. Each party warrants to the other that the signatories of this Agreement have obtained all necessary approvals or authorizations. 2. Each party warrants to the other that the signing and performance of this Agreement does not violate any other contracts, agreements, or legal documents to which it is a party. After this Agreement takes effect, no party shall claim that the signing of this Agreement did not obtain the necessary rights or violates other contracts, agreements, or legal documents to which it is a party, in order to assert this Agreement or to oppose the performance of obligations under this Agreement." Article 4 stipulated: "1. After this Agreement formally takes effect, the parties shall actively perform their relevant obligations; any act violating the provisions or warranty clauses of this Agreement shall constitute a breach of contract. 2. Compensation for the above losses shall not affect the breaching party's continued performance of this Agreement in accordance with this Agreement ..." During the first-instance trial, both parties reached a consensus that the formulas listed in the Transfer Agreement contained typographical errors and should be 50 million yuan x (1 + 6% x actual number of days of fund use / 365 days) or 50 million yuan x (1 + 8% x actual number of days of fund use / 365 days).

By December 31, 2018, no suitable third party had acquired Xing Furong's property shares in the New Energy Fund, and Dingdian Taifu Company had neither acquired the shares itself nor designated a third party to acquire them directly. On January 4, 2019, Xing Furong instructed Beijing Dacheng Law Firm to send a Lawyer's Letter to Dingdian Taifu Company, urging it to perform its obligations under the Transfer Agreement by acquiring or designating a third party to acquire Xing Furong's property shares in the New Energy Fund. On January 11, 2019, Dingdian Taifu Company sent a Response Letter to Xing Furong, Ref. No. Dingdian Taifu Han Zi [2019] No. 001, which stated: "As a fund management company, in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, regulations, and the fund partnership agreement, our company has no obligation to acquire the fund shares held by limited partners ... According to the provisions of the transfer agreement, if no suitable third party acquires your property shares by December 31, 2018, our company undertakes to acquire the shares itself or designate a third party to acquire them directly. Our company had already communicated with you before December 31, 2018 ... Our company is still willing to perform this obligation in accordance with the transfer agreement ..."

Dingdian Taifu Company is a type of other limited liability company, with Ding Shiguo as its legal representative, and its business term from November 8, 2011, to November 7, 2031. The registered capital is RMB 163 million, under a subscription system, with the capital contribution deadline of November 1, 2031. Among these, Ding Shiguo subscribed RMB 49 million, with an actual contribution of RMB 1.75 million; Dingdian Investment Company subscribed RMB 82 million, with an actual contribution of RMB 62.5 million; Jilin Investment Company subscribed RMB 30 million; and Jiaxing Zeyuan subscribed RMB 2 million, all of which have been actually contributed.

The court of first instance held that the Agreement on Transfer of Interest (the "Transfer Agreement") entered into between Xing Furong and Dingdian Taifu Company represented the true intentions of both parties, did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, was lawful and valid, and was binding on both parties, who should properly perform their respective obligations in accordance with the agreement. By December 31, 2018, no suitable third party had acquired Xing Furong's property interest, and Dingdian Taifu Company had not designated a third party to acquire such property interest. In accordance with the terms of the Transfer Agreement, the time and conditions for Dingdian Taifu Company to acquire the property interest had been fulfilled. Therefore, Xing Furong's request that Dingdian Taifu Company acquire his property interest in the partnership and pay the transfer price had factual and legal basis and was supported. When Xing Furong filed the lawsuit, he requested that Dingdian Taifu Company pay him the transfer price of RMB 74,679,452 as agreed, calculated from November 28, 2012 to January 28, 2019, and at an annual interest rate of 8% until the full transfer price is paid. After the first-instance trial, Xing Furong clarified that the amount from July 1, 2018 to the date of actual payment constituted losses for overdue payment, and claimed for such losses on the basis of RMB 50,000,000 at an interest rate of 50% above the benchmark bank loan rate for the same period. This claim did not exceed the scope of the original claims and did not constitute an increase or change of claims. Xing Furong's transfer of funds to the New Energy Fund on November 28, 2012 should be regarded as the date of actual use of the funds. The amount of the transfer price, calculated in accordance with the formula confirmed by the parties during the litigation, from November 28, 2012 to the agreed date of June 30, 2018, was: RMB 50,000,000 × (1 + 6% × 2040 days / 365 days) = RMB 66,767,123.29. Xing Furong clarified that the amount claimed from July 1, 2018 to the date of full payment of the transfer price represented losses caused to him by Dingdian Taifu Company's overdue payment. According to the Transfer Agreement, the condition for Dingdian Taifu Company to acquire Xing Furong's property interest was that no suitable third party had acquired it by December 31, 2018. Therefore, before December 31, 2018, Dingdian Taifu Company was not obliged to acquire the interest and there was no overdue payment. Xing Furong's claim for losses due to overdue payment from July 1, 2018 to December 31, 2018 had no contractual or legal basis. However, after the condition in the agreement was fulfilled on January 1, 2019, Dingdian Taifu Company failed to acquire Xing Furong's property interest and pay the transfer price as agreed, constituting a breach of contract. Xing Furong's request that Dingdian Taifu Company compensate him for losses due to overdue payment had legal basis. The court of first instance determined that the losses for overdue payment should be calculated at an annual interest rate of 6%, i.e., Dingdian Taifu Company should pay Xing Furong losses for overdue payment on the basis of RMB 50,000,000 at an annual rate of 6% from January 1, 2019 to the date of full payment of the transfer price. Xing Furong's request that Dingdian Taifu Company's shareholders Ding Shiguo, Dingdian Investment Company, Jiaxing Zeyuan, and Jilin Investment Company bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of their respective unpaid capital contributions and interest was not supported. Accordingly, the court of first instance ruled: 1. Dingdian Taifu Company shall, within ten days after the judgment becomes legally effective, pay Xing Furong a transfer price of RMB 66,767,123.29 and losses for overdue payment (on the basis of RMB 50,000,000, at an annual rate of 6%, from January 1, 2019 to the date of actual payment); 2. All other claims of Xing Furong are rejected.

During the trial of this court, Dingdian Taifu Company submitted to this court written Statements of Circumstances (Qingkuang Shuoming) issued by Jilin Province Urban Construction Industrial Co., Ltd. and Hongjia Investment Co., Ltd., limited partners of the New Energy Fund, stating that both companies did not consent to Xing Furong's transfer of his partnership interest in the New Energy Fund to Dingdian Taifu Company, purportedly to prove that the Transfer Agreement at issue was invalid for lack of consent from all partners.

Xing Furong argued in cross-examination that the above Statements of Circumstances could not affect the validity of the Transfer Agreement and could not achieve the evidentiary purpose for which Dingdian Taifu Company offered them. Ding Shiguo, Dingdian Investment Company, and Jiaxing Zeyuan argued in cross-examination that they agreed with Dingdian Taifu Company's opinion. Jilin Investment Company argued in cross-examination that the authenticity of the evidence could not be confirmed.

This court holds that the written Statements of Circumstances submitted to this court by Dingdian Taifu Company from Jilin Province Urban Construction Industrial Co., Ltd. and Hongjia Investment Co., Ltd., bearing the company seals of those entities, are objective and authentic, and their intended purpose is relevant to this case. Although Xing Furong argues that the above evidence cannot achieve its evidentiary purpose, he does not deny the authenticity of the evidence. Therefore, this court accepts the above evidence submitted by Dingdian Taifu Company. Based on this evidence, it can be determined that Jilin Province Urban Construction Industrial Co., Ltd. and Hongjia Investment Co., Ltd., the limited partners of the New Energy Fund at issue, both did not consent to Xing Furong's transfer of his partnership interest in the New Energy Fund to Dingdian Taifu Company. As for Dingdian Taifu Company's evidentiary purpose of proving the invalidity of the Transfer Agreement, this court will discuss it further below.

This court further finds: Article 29.1 of the Partnership Agreement (the "Partnership Agreement") stipulates that, subject to the consent of all partners, a limited partner may transfer all or part of its property interest in the partnership to other limited partners of the Fund or to other natural persons or legal persons meeting the conditions, provided that after the transfer, the relevant provisions of this Agreement are satisfied.

The facts found by the court of first instance are not disputed by the parties and are confirmed by this court.

This court holds that, based on the parties' allegations and defenses, the issue in dispute in this case is the validity and performance of the Transfer Agreement, which was not consented to by all partners unanimously. This issue involves the following sub-issues:

(I) The validity of the special agreement on the transfer of partnership property interests between partners.

In the legal provisions of the Partnership Enterprise Law concerning limited partnerships, there is no provision regarding the transfer of partnership property interests between partners. Article 60 of the Partnership Enterprise Law provides: "Limited partnerships and their partners shall be governed by the provisions of this Chapter; matters not covered by this Chapter shall be governed by Sections 1 to 5 of Chapter 2 of this Law concerning general partnerships and their partners." Article 22, paragraph 2 of the Partnership Enterprise Law provides for the transfer of property interests between partners in a general partnership: "When a partner transfers all or part of its property interest in the partnership to another partner, it shall notify the other partners." However, this provision does not address the validity of a special agreement in the partnership agreement on the transfer of property interests between partners. Even the forthcoming Civil Code of the PRC, in its chapter on partnership contracts, does not address the validity of special agreements on the transfer of partnership property interests between partners. Since there is a special agreement on the transfer of partnership property interests between the parties in this case, it is necessary first to determine the validity of such special agreement. In this regard, it is necessary to consider the nature of the business form or partnership organization and the legislative intent.

A partnership is a business form or organization established by two or more partners for a common business purpose, based on an agreement to share benefits and risks. The cooperation between partners is built upon a high degree of mutual trust, and thus partnership undertakings are highly personal (renhe). For example, creditors of a partner may not exercise the partner's rights by subrogation; upon the death, loss of civil capacity, or termination of a partner, the partnership contract terminates, rather than the partner's qualification or property interest being inheritable. Since partnership affairs strongly emphasize the personal element, the autonomy of the partners' will should be respected. Therefore, with respect to the transfer of property interests between partners, if there is a special agreement in the partnership agreement, and such agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, nor contravene public order and good customs, it should be deemed lawful and valid, and partners must strictly comply with it.

(II) The validity of the special agreement in the Partnership Agreement at issue concerning the transfer of partnership property interests between partners.

The New Energy Fund at issue is a limited partnership. The subject matter of the Transfer Agreement is the 19.04% property interest held by Xing Furong, a limited partner, in the New Energy Fund. Regarding the transfer of partnership property interests between partners, the Partnership Agreement at issue explicitly requires "the unanimous consent of all partners," as specifically reflected in: Article 27.6 of the Partnership Agreement, which provides that, unless otherwise agreed, the transfer or pledge of a property interest by a limited partner shall require the unanimous consent of all partners. Article 33 provides that, unless otherwise provided by law or a unanimous written decision of all partners, a limited partner may not be converted into a general partner, nor may a general partner be converted into a limited partner. This provision, applicable to the situation where Xing Furong transferred his limited partnership property interest to a general partner, further requires the unanimous consent of all partners. Article 29.1 of the agreement provides that, with the consent of all partners, a limited partner may transfer all or part of its property interest in the partnership to other limited partners of the New Energy Fund or to other natural persons or legal persons meeting the conditions, provided that after the transfer, the relevant provisions of this Agreement are satisfied. This provision further confirms the caution with which partners treat the transfer of partnership property interests. Therefore, from the above provisions of the Partnership Agreement regarding partnership property interests, it is clear that the partners of the New Energy Fund, when entering into the Partnership Agreement, based on the personal nature of partnership operations, explicitly required that the transfer of partnership property interests between partners requires the unanimous consent of all partners.

Given that the Partnership Agreement represents the true intentions of the contracting partners, the special agreement on the transfer of partnership property interests between partners in the agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, nor does it contravene public order and good customs, and is lawful and valid. Xing Furong's defense that the requirement in the Partnership Agreement for "the consent of all partners" for the transfer of property interests between partners is contrary to the provisions of the Partnership Enterprise Law and objectively restricts the legal right granted to partners by the Partnership Enterprise Law to transfer property interests, and therefore the agreement is not binding on the parties, lacks legal basis. Moreover, as stated above, this reasoning is precisely contrary to the spirit of high autonomy of partners emphasized by the personal nature of the partnership business form or organization, and thus this court does not accept it.

(III) The validity and performance of the Transfer Agreement at issue.

The Transfer Agreement at issue was entered into between Xing Furong and Dingdian Taifu Company and represents the true intentions of Xing Furong and Dingdian Taifu Company. In accordance with Article 25 of the Contract Law of the PRC, which provides: "A contract is formed when the offer and acceptance become effective," the Transfer Agreement was formed when the parties reached mutual consent. However, given that the Partnership Agreement at issue explicitly requires the unanimous consent of all partners for the transfer of partnership property interests between partners, for the Transfer Agreement to become effective, the condition of unanimous consent of all partners must still be satisfied. Before the other partners have expressly consented to the transfer of the partnership property interest, the Transfer Agreement at issue is in a state of being formed but not yet effective. During the trial of this case, Jilin Province Urban Construction Industrial Co., Ltd. and Hongjia Investment Co., Ltd., the limited partners of the New Energy Fund, submitted written Statements of Circumstances to this court, both expressly stating that they do not consent to Xing Furong's transfer of his partnership property interest to Dingdian Taifu Company. This fact demonstrates that the Transfer Agreement, concerning the transfer of the partnership property interest, has definitively failed to obtain the consent of all partners. Therefore, the Transfer Agreement is definitively ineffective and cannot create an obligation of performance between the parties.

In this lawsuit, Xing Furong's claim for performance of the Transfer Agreement is premised on the Transfer Agreement being lawful, valid, and enforceable. Given that the Transfer Agreement has definitively become ineffective, Xing Furong's claim for performance of the Transfer Agreement lacks factual and legal basis and should be rejected. The court of first instance's determination that the Transfer Agreement at issue was lawful and valid, and its ruling that Dingdian Taifu Company should continue to perform the agreement, violates the common intention expressed in the Partnership Agreement that the transfer of partnership property interests requires the unanimous consent of all partners, and also violates the common intention expressed in the Partnership Agreement that a limited partner cannot be converted into a general partner, nor a general partner into a limited partner, without the unanimous consent of all partners. The first-instance judgment erred in fact-finding and application of law and should be corrected.

Dingdian Taifu Company argues that the Transfer Agreement at issue is invalid, while this court finds that the Transfer Agreement is ineffective and there are no grounds for invalidity. From the perspective of the result, the legal effect that a contract that is definitively ineffective lacks enforceability is the same as that of a void contract lacking enforceability — in both cases, the legal consequence is that Xing Furong's claim for continued performance of the Transfer Agreement cannot be sustained. Therefore, Dingdian Taifu Company's appellate argument that Xing Furong's claim for continued performance of the Transfer Agreement and payment of the transfer price should be rejected is well-founded and supported by this court.

As for Dingdian Taifu Company's other appellate arguments, they are also essentially negating Xing Furong's claims and can be encompassed by this court's rejection of Xing Furong's claims. Therefore, since this court has corrected the first-instance judgment and rejected Xing Furong's claims, there is no need for this court to further examine Dingdian Taifu Company's other appellate arguments.

In conclusion, Dingdian Taifu Company's appeal is sustained, and Xing Furong's claims should be rejected. The first-instance judgment contains errors in fact-finding and application of law and should be corrected. In accordance with Article 170, paragraph 1(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this court rules as follows:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2019) Ji Min Chu No. 5 of the Jilin High People's Court;

2. Reject Xing Furong's claims.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 415,198, preservation fee of RMB 5,000, and second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 375,635.62 are all to be borne by Xing Furong.

This judgment is final.
